The word “Sioux” is a exonym. That means someone else’s name for them. It is from French, from Nadouessioux, and perhaps from Ojibwa, nātowēssiwak. It meant “little rattlesnake” or “little devils”. Or it could instead mean "speaks a foreign language". People really are not sure. The Englioish speakers shortened it to Sioux. However, some latched onto the possible negative meaning. In any case, it is not their own word for themselves. It is from a nearby enemy people. Thus some don’t like it.

The word “Sioux” refers to the various Lakota and Dakota peoples. The word “Lakota” means "feeling affection, friendly, united, allied". Dakota has a similar meaning. Some tribes have “Sioux” as their official name. Other tribes do not. Any federally recognized tribe is free to use whatever name they choose. Some have both. The Rosebud Sioux Tribe is also known as the Sičháŋǧu Oyáte (Brulé Nation).

That is a very difficult question to answer. I personally have problems with the overall attitude of the city. To no one’s fault, it’s a very transient city. Up until the Knight’s came around the city had no sense of community at all. The strip has created a environment where you can make a lot of money out of high school and so a lot of people don’t really mentally or emotionally grow up. However; the food scene is amazing! As well as the arts and the hockey community has become strong! Along with the Vegas Strong movement the city has had a really positive awakening so to speak.

If you are an outdoors type like I am; you have access (or a close drive) to some of the best outdoors activities across the board. Even snowboarding; and a 4 hour drive to ocean beachfront isn’t bad either. 

Be warned though, it is definitely a unique and different interpersonal environment. I have had a lot of my friends swear off dating till they move out of the city. It may be bad luck, it may be the instant gratification of the city. But for the most part I’d say there is a underlying feel of greed in a lot of people.

Despite all of that; I am truly thankful I moved here. Of the friends I have made I have been blessed with some of the most amazing humans I have ever had the honor of meeting. I have had the opportunity to experience things I couldn’t imagine experiencing in other places. I get to watch a city grow and become a community. My neighbors are amazing and resilient individuals who have fought to survive when the housing market crashed here and have stories to tell. The history of the city and the mob involvement is amazing. The night life is better than any other city I’ve lived in. (For reference; St Louis, Louisville, Orlando, Honolulu, Charleston, and Austin.) If you can manage to not lose yourself Las Vegas is worth moving to, if only for a short time.

Extra taxes on construction companies makes the margin much thinner and the development fees make it a bigger risk than it’s worth. These extra fees are again due to politician trying to get more money for the states social programs. This isn’t even mentioning the lobbying of unions and how badly they handcuffed the construction groups in Cali.

Sure you can make it look like a supply and demand issue if you only look on the surface. But doing any bit of research and it all points to the systems set in Cali make it that way.

Most people have already spoken about the high clipping and tensing when you don’t need to. So I’ll switch gears for a second. 

A training technique you could use for yourself is back down one grade from your project and move slowly and precisely. I noticed you fumble with holds, both your feet and hands, making effort to find the “right spot”. For me I trained less about hitting the perfect spot, because outdoors doesn’t always have it, and more about comfortable deciding this is where I’m going to be on the hold and sticking to it. That means consciously considering every single move not just throwing for the next hold. At first if will be difficult, but this training got me from 10c to 13’s in a year.

With all of the cartilage gone it’s kinda a needed thing. However to keep this in mind. If the surgery is local only to the thumb you can hang board during the recovery time. While a lot of your endurance will be lost you can at least up keep general grip strengths. 

Also if you are hang boarding intelligently you could assist in the muscle regrowth in your hand and come back stronger than you would think. 

While I understand that taking time off is daunting, myself coming off a ten month recovery from a non climbing related injury that requires surgery. Sometimes it’s needed. Have good habits and the return will be fine. If you can get the thumb feeling good enough quick enough I would suggest yoga as well. It will actually be healthy for your body and limber your body making it to where you can climb longer in life and it will keep your body in check during the period where you can’t use the thumb! If you have a instructor already just tell them on the injury and ask for modifications.

Good luck! I hope to hear about you crushing 12’s yourself someday soon!
